links.outcome: Performance of GON detection AI across different hospitals and image quality levels
links.effect: Accuracy 93.18% at the development hospital (QHSDU) and 91.40% at three other hospitals; AUC 95.17% and 96.64%; sensitivity 91.75% and 91.41%.
links.quote: With acceptable generalization capability across varying levels of image quality, different clinical centres, or certain retinal comorbidities, such as HM, the automatic AI diagnostic system had the potential to provide expert-level glaucoma detection.

links.outcome: Performance in a new population (high myopia) beyond the original use context
links.effect: In the high myopia subset, accuracy was 81.98% and AUC 87.49% (sensitivity 83.61%, specificity 81.76%), lower than the 93.18% accuracy and 95.17% AUC in dataset 1.
links.quote: In validation dataset 3, the algorithm achieved comparable accuracy of 81.98% and AUC of 87.49%, with a sensitivity of 83.61% and specificity of 81.76% on GON recognition specifically in the HM population.

screen.reason: Multicenter external validation of an automated AI system for detecting glaucomatous optic neuropathy on fundus photographs across multiple cohorts and comorbidity subgroups.
